message:
From: CEO Name <hacker@gmail.com>
Subject: Urgent Wire Transfer
Please process the attached wire transfer before close of business. Keep this strictly confidential and do not discuss it.
suspicious: hacker@gmail.com; urgent; wire transfer; strictly confidential; do not discuss
red_flags: Display-name/domain mismatch; executive impersonation; urgency; secrecy; financial request; bypass of normal verification
why: The visible executive identity conflicts with the real sender domain, while urgency and secrecy are used to suppress independent verification. A wire-transfer request should be verified through a trusted, separate channel.

message:
From: Account Security <security@yourcompany-secure-login.com>
Subject: Verify your account
Your account will be disabled today. Sign in now to restore access.
suspicious: yourcompany-secure-login.com; disabled today; sign in now; restore access
red_flags: Lookalike/combosquatting domain; urgency; credential-harvesting language; unsolicited login request
why: The root domain is not the legitimate company domain. The threat of immediate disablement is a cognitive pressure tactic designed to make the recipient click without checking the destination.

message:
From: DecodeLabs Support <support@www.decodelabs.tech.login-update.com>
Subject: Login update required
Confirm your credentials at the link below to keep your account active.
suspicious: www.decodelabs.tech.login-update.com; login update; confirm your credentials; keep active
red_flags: Nested subdomain trap; misleading trusted-name prefix; credential request; urgency/continuity pressure
why: Reading the address from right to left reveals login-update.com as the true root domain. The trusted brand appears only as a subdomain, which is a classic deceptive URL construction.

message:
From: Security Alert <no-reply@security-alert.example>
Subject: Unusual sign-in detected
We detected a suspicious login. Click the link immediately to secure your account.
suspicious: unusual sign-in; suspicious login; click immediately; secure your account
red_flags: Alarmist activity alert; direct login link; urgency; unknown sender/domain; no manual-navigation advice
why: A fake security alert can redirect users to a phishing login page. The safer approach is to navigate manually to the known service rather than use an unsolicited link.

message:
From: IT Security <it-security@example.com>
Subject: MFA Verification Required
Reply with your MFA code and confirm your password so we can complete the security check.
suspicious: MFA Verification Required; MFA code; confirm your password; security check
red_flags: Unexpected MFA/password request; credential harvesting; impersonation of IT; sensitive information request
why: Legitimate support processes should not ask users to disclose passwords or one-time MFA codes by email. Providing them can enable account takeover.

message:
From: Subscription Billing <billing@example.net>
Subject: Subscription renewal issue
Your payment failed. Call 1-800-555-0199 immediately to cancel the charge.
suspicious: payment failed; call immediately; cancel the charge; 1-800-555-0199
red_flags: Callback scam; fake billing problem; urgency; phone number as the main action; no trusted navigation path
why: The message avoids a clickable malicious link but uses a phone number to move the victim into a social-engineering conversation. The number should not be trusted merely because the email looks official.

message:
From: Google Account Team <alert@example.net>
Subject: Account recovery required
Scan the QR code within 30 minutes to prevent your account from being locked.
suspicious: scan the QR code; within 30 minutes; prevent account lock; account recovery
red_flags: Unsolicited QR code; urgency; account-lock threat; bypasses desktop URL inspection
why: QR codes can send users to phishing pages on a mobile device where the destination is harder to inspect. The time limit is intended to discourage verification.

message:
From: Project Manager <sarah.lee@company.com>
Subject: Q3 Project Status
Please review the attached Q3_Status.html immediately and enable content if prompted.
red_flags: HTML attachment; potentially executable/redirecting content; pressure to open; enable-content instruction
why: HTML files can be used to redirect or stage credential theft, and instructions to enable content increase the risk. Unexpected HTML attachments should be isolated and verified.

message:
From: Executive Office <exec-update@example.net>
Subject: FW: FW: Confidential Payment Approval
Pasted prior messages contain odd timestamps and headers. Please approve the payment today.
suspicious: FW: FW:; confidential; approve today; odd timestamps/headers
red_flags: Fake forwarded chain; inconsistent timestamps; unfamiliar thread; financial request; urgency
why: Artificial forwarding history can make a fraudulent request appear established. The unusual headers and timestamps warrant independent verification before any payment action.

message:
From: Project Manager <sarah.lee@company.com>
Subject: Q3 Project Status Update - Non-Urgent
Please review the attached project status for Q3 at your earliest convenience. No immediate action is required.
red_flags: No strong phishing indicators in the supplied sample; still verify the attachment through normal procedures
why: This is a control sample from the project brief: it explicitly states that no immediate action is required and does not request credentials, payment, secrecy, or bypassing procedure. Normal attachment-safety checks still apply.
